verifier_note: Checked against: rustc 1.98.1 stable docs (u128 checked_mul/div/rem, Cargo overflow-checks, operator-expr overflow, the wasm32-unknown-unknown platform page), all retrieved live via WebFetch; midly 0.5.3 src/primitive.rs read from the local cargo registry and cross-checked live on docs.rs (byte-identical: u15/u24 masks, Timing::Metrical doc comments); the signed si-jam-sessions Phase 0 lock fetched at its pinned commit e3cc85e via the GitHub API for every engine_note; the compile oracle run over the whole lane (6/6 checks PASS, exact stdout); and independent Python bigint recomputation of every numeric claim in recipes 1-4 (all 8 tuplet levels at 4 PPQs, the u128 overflow bound and its 2.44e19-day floor, the carried-remainder equality at 4 PPQs), plus one original counter-example (tick=tempo=1e15, ppq=1) proving recipe 5s u64-quotient-overflow refusal path is real and distinct from its tested ppq=0 path, with no panic. Nothing failed; all five are confirmed and solid, and PHASE-0.md explicitly cites two of these five findings (PPQ 3360s tuplet-exactness, the tick-to-sample formula) as already verified by this KB. Systemic weakness: every check in this lane is self-referential -- the same Rust program both derives and asserts its numbers, so a shared conceptual error in the generators arithmetic would compile and pass silently; the only real guard is a verifier reimplementing the arithmetic independently, which is what this pass did in Python rather than re-trusting the compilers rerun of the same code. A second, smaller weakness: 4 of 5 recipes lean on one page (doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/primitive.u128.html) for their core API warrant, so that single page is a concentration point for the whole lanes Rust-currency claim.
